blind_review.scope_warning: The deterministic sample is 100 selected rows from 43 restaurants in one Pacific development market; it is not a national yield estimate.

accepted_implementation_fixes: Terminal review now locks the attempt and photo and rejects a second review.
Terminal review requires exact stored display-only Customer consent.
First server receipt wins for one attempt/event/source.
Upload replay compares restaurant, menu item, visitor, session, experiment, variant, surface, and target class.
The supplied isolated fixture demonstrated a positive approval, stored-consent rejection, exact Customer/Management duplicate rejection, a failed-gold case, and one receipt-concurrency case.
blocking_findings: Exporter, runtime prompt eligibility, and the SQL gold predicate are not one canonical contract.
Exporter provenance is hard-coded false and can evaluate a different selected photo than the SQL function.
Rights have no independent review/audit gate, and source-snapshot lineage is not tightly bound to entity and source.
Runtime behavioral eligibility does not verify the latest successful source snapshot even though the exported gate says it does.
The 54-row selected-photo ledger does not reproduce the 4876-to-4882 population correction or explain the 3912-to-3881 snapshot drift.
All-photo selection omits several provenance and duplicate gates, so a lower fully passing photo can remain hidden.

Fixture claims exceed the tests: real exporter-to-SQL parity, rejected-review replay, full database cross-target replay, each gold-gate failure, and route-level receipt concurrency are not demonstrated.
A failed upload can retry under the same attempt while immutable failure receipts suppress a later success.
Public traffic has no positive eligible_external path, so a live treatment would have no claimable external denominator.
